The plan puts the fix in the right place: `Drain::finish`'s unconditional `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure)` at drain.rs 2379 is where the fault starts. Splitting a landing error by where it arises (`landing_from_report` Ok vs Err at 3052/3056) and reusing `StopCause::of` (disk.rs 388-415) are both sound. The demonstrations name real seams (`drain::drain` with `Stub`, plus the production `landing_from_report`), and each would fail under the old rule. One part of the classification is a guess the code contradicts. The plan treats every `Err` from `RealSteps::run` (3562) and from a read (3510) as a shared host or Athena cause. Its risk section says those Err arms "carry host and Athena errors, as their code shows". They do not. `go_with_stages` bails with errors about the item's own job state ('job X was declined', 'is already closed', 'is running', 'was interrupted', at run/mod.rs 340-360), and pin.rs 150 bails with 'job X has N readings, the most a job may have'. Once names and digits are masked, two unrelated items hitting the same one of these sentences get identical keys and stop the batch. That is the same false-shared fault the request is about. A shared cause needs evidence that it is shared, not just "no outcome". I checked the code with Read and Grep only and ran nothing. Findings: major: Every run or read Err is classed as a shared cause, but many Err texts are verdicts on the item's own job. After masking they match across items and would stop the batch falsely.
